ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy May ’69 show hampered by muddy cassette soundboard
ai_show_review.blurb: The band delivered a spirited, high‑energy set on May 29 1969, but the tape sounds like it was copied twice and is very muffed. Jerry was visibly frustrated with the weak PA, and the overall listening experience suffers from the poor recording quality.
ai_show_review.review: On May 29, 1969 at Robertson Gym, U.C.S.B., the Dead took the stage with a classic late‑60s lineup that included Pigpen and Tom Constanten on keys. The performance itself was lively and full of the raw enthusiasm typical of that era, but the only surviving recording is a cassette‑generation soundboard capture that sounds “skeevy,” muffled, and lacking clarity. Reviewers note Jerry Garcia’s frustration as he struggled to hear his own drums through the sub‑par PA, even walking off briefly in irritation. While the band kept the energy high, the audio limitations make this show more of a historical curiosity than a listening recommendation for most fans.

best_recording.reason: Only known source; despite poor quality it captures the full show and is the sole reference for this performance.
